description: Two-panel composite figure combining a scatter/linear-fit plot with a stacked bar chart of strengthening contributions. (a) plots the true flow stress at yielding sigma_F0 (y axis, MPa, 340-480 in 20 MPa steps) against the inverse square root of the mean effective grain size d_e^-1/2 (x axis, micrometre^-1/2, 0.20-0.40 in 0.04 steps) for the hot-rolled steel states; open squares are labelled sigma_F0 and the red line is labelled "Hall-Petch fitting". Three points carry printed coordinates: 359.5 MPa at d_e = 21.82 micrometre, 420.0 MPa at 11.55 micrometre, and 479.3 MPa at 7.02 micrometre. A dashed box in (a) prints the fitted relation sigma_F0 = sigma_y - sigma_p - sigma_ds = 203.1 + 733.4 d_e^-1/2. (b) is a stacked bar chart of calculated yield-strength contributions (Stress, MPa, 0-800 in 100 MPa steps) for the rolling states HR45, HR68 and HR82, with segments sigma_gb (solid blue), sigma_ds (blue hatch), sigma_p-Orowan (red), sigma_p-shearing (pink) and sigma_F (cross-hatch), plus open triangles marking sigma_exp. Stack totals rise monotonically HR45 < HR68 < HR82 (HR45 just below 500 MPa, HR82 above 600 MPa), with sigma_gb the largest segment and a nearly constant sigma_F base near 200 MPa. Together the panels argue that effective-grain-size grain-boundary strengthening dominates the yield-strength gain from increasing hot-rolling reduction.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of true flow stress at yielding sigma_F0 (MPa) versus d_e^-1/2 (micrometre^-1/2) with three open-square data points labelled 359.5 MPa / 21.82 micrometre, 420.0 MPa / 11.55 micrometre and 479.3 MPa / 7.02 micrometre, fitted by a red line labelled 'Hall-Petch fitting'; a dashed inset box gives sigma_F0 = sigma_y - sigma_p - sigma_ds = 203.1 + 733.4 d_e^-1/2.

Stacked bar chart of calculated strengthening contributions to yield strength (Stress, MPa, 0-800) for HR45, HR68 and HR82 rolling states, stacked in order sigma_F (cross-hatched), sigma_p-shearing (pink), sigma_p-Orowan (red), sigma_ds (blue hatch) and sigma_gb (solid blue), with open triangles labelled sigma_exp slightly above each bar total; bar totals increase from HR45 to HR82.

observations.observation: Panel (a) contains exactly three data points printed with coordinates: 359.5 MPa (d_e = 21.82 micrometre), 420.0 MPa (d_e = 11.55 micrometre) and 479.3 MPa (d_e = 7.02 micrometre).
The red line in (a) is labelled 'Hall-Petch fitting' and rises monotonically with d_e^-1/2, passing through the three open-square points.
The dashed inset box in (a) prints the equation sigma_F0 = sigma_y - sigma_p - sigma_ds = 203.1 + 733.4 d_e^-1/2.
The x axis of (a) is d_e^-1/2 with unit micrometre^-1/2 over 0.20-0.40, and the y axis is sigma_F0 in MPa over 340-480.
Panel (b) legend entries are sigma_gb, sigma_ds, sigma_p-Orowan, sigma_p-shearing, sigma_F and sigma_exp (triangle), with the bars grouped by rolling state HR45, HR68, HR82.
In (b) the sigma_gb segment is the largest single contribution in every bar, and the cross-hatched sigma_F base is nearly the same height in all three bars.
Stacked bar totals in (b) increase in the order HR45 < HR68 < HR82; HR45 stays just below the 500 MPa gridline while HR82 exceeds the 600 MPa gridline.

The caption states that sigma in (a) is the true flow stress at yielding obtained by subtracting precipitate strengthening sigma_p and dislocation strengthening sigma_ds from the yield strength sigma_y.
The caption states that the triangles in (b) indicate the experimentally tested results.
The citing text names the quantity plotted in (a) and in the inset equation as sigma_F0, whereas the caption calls it sigma; the two labels refer to the same plotted quantity.

The citing text reports a friction stress sigma_0 of 203.10 MPa (y-axis intercept) and a Hall-Petch coefficient k_HP of 733.43 MPa micrometre^1/2 (slope), consistent with the 203.1 and 733.4 printed in the inset of (a).
The citing text reports grain-boundary strengthening contributions of 157.02 MPa (HR45), 215.84 MPa (HR68) and 276.78 MPa (HR82), which correspond to the increasing blue sigma_gb segments in (b).

The citing text states that grain-boundary strengthening from HAGBs plus annealing twin boundaries was the predominant mechanism and dislocation strengthening was also prominent, responsible for the yield-strength increase with hot-rolling reduction.
The citing text states that the calculated contributions in Fig. 9(b) are summarized in Table 2 and show good consistency with the experimental results.
